title: Ingo Swann affects shielded quark detector at SRI

tellings.quote: we had the cork detector and so it was basically a quantum chip inside a new metal magnetic shielding inside of steel dewar for electrical shielding inside of superconducting shielding the requirement being that nothing could affect this thing from the outside so we want to see if you can affect it he affected it unequivocally 100 percent
In 1972, laser physicist Hal Puthoff was doing experiments with New York City-based psychic Ingo Swann.
tellings.difference: Told by the host rather than by Puthoff firsthand. Dates it to 1972 and calls Swann New York City-based.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Ingo Swann affecting a shielded detector in Hal Puthoff's early-1970s experiments.

as_told.title: Ingo Swann remote views a shielded detector for Hal Puthoff

related.note: The same early-1970s SRI test of Swann affecting a shielded device with Puthoff, but here the device is a thermistor in a Faraday cage rather than a shielded quark detector.

plain: The laser physicist Hal Puthoff says that at the Stanford Research Institute in the early 1970s, the psychic Ingo Swann changed the readings of a quark detector, a sensitive quantum chip sealed inside layers of magnetic shielding, a steel flask and superconducting shielding so that "nothing could affect this thing from the outside", and that Swann "affected it unequivocally, 100 percent". Puthoff tells Michels this as the experimenter who ran it; Michels, in an earlier episode, sets the work in 1972 and calls Swann a New York City psychic. If true, it would mean a mind can act on shielded matter at a distance.
